title: arXiv Trending AI — Daily — 2026-11-02
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart or readership/download ranking; this is an inferred relevance-ranked shortlist, and citation evidence is limited for these recent papers.

sections.title: Latent Sparse Attention: Towards Subquadratic Ultra-Long Context Attention
sections.abstract: The paper introduces hierarchical latent-space key clustering for sparse attention, reporting faster prefill, decode, and training at long contexts while maintaining similar evaluated accuracy.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose Distilled-LSA for adapting pretrained models and Native-LSA for native training; the abstract reports up to 72.4× prefill and 42.5× decode speedups over full attention for one evaluated layer at 10M tokens on QWEN-3.8-27B.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors note that LSA does not reduce KV-cache storage, which still grows linearly with context. Native LSA was evaluated at about 0.5B parameters and up to 128k tokens; scaling native training and tree search remains open.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Tests up to 10M tokens and compares prefill/decode performance against sparse and full attention; direct systems contribution to the long-context bottleneck.

sections.title: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
sections.abstract: LARC trains unified multimodal models to reason over continuous hidden states, reporting improved text-to-image quality and test-time scaling on several generation benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine curriculum supervised fine-tuning with information-gain reinforcement learning to move reasoning into the continuous latent space used for image generation; they report a 7 percentage-point GenEval gain over BAGEL.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper notes that latent reasoning traces are not human-interpretable and lack direct ground-truth annotations; evaluation is centered on the reported model and benchmark setup.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across three core AI categories; arXiv record says it was published as a NeurIPS 2026 conference proceeding. Evaluates three text-to-image benchmarks and reports test-time scaling.

sections.title: In-Model Context Compression with Agentic Soft Tokens for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
sections.abstract: ASTC uses a model's recurrent dynamics to preserve absorbed context as soft tokens while retaining exact values as hard tokens, reporting up to 50.68% fewer end-to-end attention pairs on long-horizon tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors present a training-free, model-native context compression method that reuses recurrent state and carries it forward as soft tokens, with reusable KV caches across an agent trajectory.
sections.unique_caveat: The method is built around hybrid Gated Delta Network–attention dynamics; the abstract does not establish that the same compression behavior transfers to other model architectures.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Four core-category listings and a code repository linked from the arXiv record; reports task-level attention-pair savings against uncompressed agents and trained compressors.

sections.title: RoboArchitect: Automating the Design of Robotic Agents with Persistent Memory
sections.abstract: RoboArchitect uses a coding model to inspect robot rollouts and iteratively revise the control harness around a frozen policy, reporting higher success on held-out scenes and tasks without changing model weights.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors show an iterative harness-optimization loop that diagnoses failures, edits control code, and retains learned experience as persistent memory; they report improved average success on held-out scenes and tasks.
sections.unique_caveat: Results are from the reported manipulation benchmarks and held-out splits; they do not establish unrestricted transfer to arbitrary robots, tasks, or deployment conditions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in robotics, AI, and vision, with a project website linked from the arXiv record. Reported comparisons span multiple benchmarks and policies and use held-out scenes/tasks.

sections.title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
sections.abstract: ID-WM separates high-level reachable-subgoal selection from low-level action generation and reports gains over policy, diffusion-planning, and single-level world-model baselines on navigation and manipulation suites.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose a hierarchical world model that samples feasible transitions at a high level and grounds them through a low-level inverse-dynamics model; they report improved long-horizon planning over the compared baselines.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that search in diffusion latent space increases inference time and that planning still scales with state-space dimensionality.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in robotics and AI; evaluates three navigation/manipulation suites and includes a vision-based long-horizon planning comparison.

sections.title: Erase the Injected Region: Multimodal Prompt-Injection Defense with On-Policy Self-Distillation
sections.abstract: ERASE trains a model on attacked media to imitate a frozen base model viewing the same media with the injected region blanked, reporting low observed attack success while retaining task utility on evaluated image, audio, and video tests.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce an on-policy self-distillation defense that replaces the injected region with modality-appropriate blank content in the teacher view while preserving surrounding task-relevant media.
sections.unique_caveat: Near-zero attack success is reported on the evaluated benchmarks and models; this is not a guarantee against untested adaptive attacks or deployment inputs.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in AI and security; tests three input modalities and two model sizes, reporting both attack resistance and task utility.

sections.title: TraceSpec: Understanding and Improving Speculative Decoding for LLM Agents
sections.abstract: TraceSpec analyzes speculative decoding by agent trajectory phase and trains a state-conditioned draft strategy, reporting 12.5–22.6% higher replay throughput than its DSpark base across browsing and software-engineering workloads.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors connect trajectory-conditioned evaluation with adaptive draft training, using intermediate assistant turns and predicted acceptance gaps to allocate a fixed prediction budget.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported throughput gains are from replay evaluations on browsing and software-engineering traces; the abstract does not establish the same gains for other agent workloads or live serving.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Contributes a 10,000-state training and 2,500-state test resource and evaluates three target sizes and two temperatures; focus is the agent-call workload.

sections.title: When Does Test-Time Search Help World Action Models? An Empirical Audit of Candidate Selection and Simulator Integrity
sections.abstract: A preregistered audit of Cosmos Policy and RoboCasa finds little exploitable signal for candidate selection, modest end-to-end speedups from token pruning, and a simulator-rendering corruption that can distort evaluation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors test candidate-selection signal, realized efficiency, and evaluation integrity as separate premises for test-time scaling, and report a detector and fix for a silent rendering-corruption issue.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors explicitly scope their conclusions to the tested configuration; the results do not settle whether test-time search helps other world-action models or environments.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Provides a preregistered audit with a simulator-integrity check and reports negative as well as positive results on two named setups, useful counterpoint to claims of test-time planning gains.
